title: October 28 — Evening: scouts write material, waves read histories, heredity is tested
summary: BlackBoxLab's Cell 0 scout writer meets the finite-speed ping-reader idea explored by WallMemoryLaw. In 48 pre-registered order-test worlds, 16 and 8 pings classify writing order 1.000, outperforming the global material mean (0.625), but shuffled/phase-scrambled maps classify just as well: this reader hears the distribution of amounts, not their spatial arrangement. A separate recency gate fails. The material→ping→child read-write loop does not preserve two stable types: seek-first dominates; a designed quorum only delays loss of avoid-first. Averaging evidence before thresholding or writing two positive signals is an untested next gate.

nodes.claim: Cell 0 scouts copied from BlackBoxLab write a slowly retained bulk material mass into a Klein–Gordon field. After the scouts vanish, fixed source–receiver wave pings read the frozen medium's history; a second experiment uses local ping decisions as the only parent-to-child channel to test physical-medium heredity.
nodes.survived: Pre-registered equal-total writing-order test on 48 fresh worlds: 16 and 8 broadband pings each classify seek→avoid versus avoid→seek at LOO 1.000 (2000-shuffle p floor 0.0005); one ping gets 0.833, while scalar mean material gets 0.625. Finite-speed elliptical footprints pass Gate 0. Phase-scrambling and pixel-shuffling keep order accuracy at 1.000, establishing readable value-distribution differences rather than necessary spatial-layout information.
nodes.killed: The harder 32-world recency ping test fails (0.625; p=0.18), while mean material alone achieves 0.812, correcting an earlier 12-world claim. In material→ping→children lineages, 0/8 pure avoid-first lines survive eight generations under single receptors (8/8 seek-first); nine-vote quorum retains only 2/8 avoid-first (8/8 seek-first). No bistable heredity, genetic reproduction, geometry-specific arrangement decoding, real physical hardware or theorem-level physical inheritance is demonstrated; multi-ping and two-presence rescues are predictions, not experiments.
nodes.era: October 28: external observation and inheritance in written media

edges.why: Evening copies BlackBoxLab's Cell 0 writer code and the seek/avoid schedule protocol; it replaces the earlier god's-eye map observer with an independent wave-ping readout.

Evening tests a finite-speed source→material→receiver observation footprint inspired by WallMemoryLaw's causal scattering tours, but changes from externally written boundary patches to scout-written distributed Klein–Gordon mass; this is a conceptual/method transfer, not a fork or validation of wall-calibration scaling.

motifs.title: A wave can read a written history without the god's-eye map
motifs.description: BlackBoxLab Cell 0 supplies local scouts that write persistent bulk material; WallMemoryLaw supplies a finite-travel-time interrogation idea. Evening connects them: a blind ping hears writing-order signatures in the distribution of material amounts, with footprint and shuffle controls. This is a genuine external observer but does not yet read fine spatial arrangement or prove a cheaper physical memory than direct material statistics.

motifs.title: A self-read/write loop can select a winner without inheriting two states
motifs.description: Evening's only intergenerational channel is a material field measured by local pings. Seek-first spreads into avoid-first lineages because its signature survives contamination; pure avoid-first is fragile. The one-bit code contracts toward seek-first under the tested receptor, while stronger analog evidence averaging and two positive materials remain falsifiable proposals.
